_**Sleep Is the Enemy**_ is the third studio album by Canadian rock band Danko Jones. The album was released on February 17, 2006 in Europe and February 21 in Canada. The album was released in the US on May 23. "She's Drugs" was featured in the Swedish vampire film _Frostbiten_. "Baby Hates Me" served as the theme song for _WWE Backlash_.

# In This Moment Release New Song “Sleeping with the Enemy”
### _The band’s last album ‘Godmode’ came out back in 2023_
_In This Moment [Courtesy]_
In This Moment are back with a brand new song “Sleeping with the Enemy.” The track follows the previously released “Heretic” featuring Kim Dracula. Both songs will be featured on the band’s upcoming new album, which follows their 2023 LP _Godmode_.
Stream the official music video for “Sleeping with the Enemy” below.
Back in March, singer Maria Brink made a special guest appearance on the latest Eva Under Fire single “Villainous.” It is the title track to the band’s forthcoming album that arrives on July 10.
In 2022, In This Moment released the single “Blood 1983,” a collaboration with Spencer Charnas of Ice Nine Kills, which blended synthwave influences with the band’s signature heavy sound and demonstrated their willingness to experiment stylistically while remaining commercially relevant in active rock radio.
In 2023, In This Moment released their eighth studio album,_Godmode_, another collaboration with producer Kane Churko. The album leaned further into industrial and electronic textures while maintaining the aggressive riffs and cinematic atmosphere that had defined the band’s later career. Songs such as “The Purge,” “Army of Me,” and “Damaged” reinforced themes of empowerment, trauma, identity, and resilience that had long been central to Brink’s lyricism. Around the same time, the band embarked on another successful edition of their annual “The Dark Horizon Tour,” co-headlining with Motionless in White and performing at major rock festivals across North America. _In This Moment [Courtesy]_
In This Moment are back with a brand new song “Sleeping with the Enemy.” The track follows the previously released “Heretic” featuring Kim Dracula. Both songs will be featured on the band’s upcoming new album, which follows their 2023 LP _Godmode_.
Stream the official music video for “Sleeping with the Enemy” below.
Back in March, singer Maria Brink made a special guest appearance on the latest Eva Under Fire single “Villainous.” It is the title track to the band’s forthcoming album that arrives on July 10.
In 2022, In This Moment released the single “Blood 1983,” a collaboration with Spencer Charnas of Ice Nine Kills, which blended synthwave influences with the band’s signature heavy sound and demonstrated their willingness to experiment stylistically while remaining commercially relevant in active rock radio.
In 2023, In This Moment released their eighth studio album,_Godmode_, another collaboration with producer Kane Churko. The album leaned further into industrial and electronic textures while maintaining the aggressive riffs and cinematic atmosphere that had defined the band’s later career. Songs such as “The Purge,” “Army of Me,” and “Damaged” reinforced themes of empowerment, trauma, identity, and resilience that had long been central to Brink’s lyricism. Around the same time, the band embarked on another successful edition of their annual “The Dark Horizon Tour,” co-headlining with Motionless in White and performing at major rock festivals across North America. Their ability to balance mainstream hard rock appeal with gothic imagery and metal influences helped them maintain a loyal fanbase while attracting younger listeners through streaming platforms and social media exposure.

**Danko Jones** is a Canadian hard rock band formed in Toronto in 1996, now residing in Stockholm. The band consists of vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones, bassist John "JC" Calabrese and drummer Rich Knox, with Jones and Calabrese remaining the band's only continuous members.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-birch-1) The band's musical style includes elements of hard rock and punk, and they are known for their extensive touring and high-energy live performances, which has earned them acclaim as one of the best live acts in rock music.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-noise-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-3) Danko Jones has released eleven studio albums and been nominated for six Juno Awards.

### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
[edit]
The band was formed in 1996 by Danko Jones (Rishi Ganjoo), Scaltro (John Calabrese) and Gran Sfigato (Michael Caricari), after the former's namesake and initially named Danko Jones And The Impossible Dream.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-:0-5) Danko Jones played consistently for two years after formation in and around the northeastern United States and Canada, opening for The New Bomb Turks, Nashville Pussy, Blonde Redhead, The Make-Up, The Dirtbombs, The Chrome Cranks, and The Demolition Doll Rods. Originally they did not intend to release an album, preferring to have the band's live reputation spread by word of mouth.
Eventually, the trio relented and put out a self-titled six-song EP on Sonic Unyon records in 1998. In 1999, the band performed around Toronto, including at Lee's Palace[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-6) and the Horseshoe Tavern.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-7) That year they released the self-produced _My Love Is Bold_ E.P. and release the single "Bounce". They were nominated for a Juno Award in 2000 for Best Alternative Album.
In early 2000, Danko Jones opened for Beck at Maple Leaf Gardens.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-8) In 2001, Bad Taste Records released a compilation of the band's early recordings, demos, and b-sides entitled, _[I'm Alive and On Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_Alive\_and\_On\_Fire "I'm Alive and On Fire")_. A five-week European tour followed to promote the release including shows at the Roskilde festival in Denmark and Hultsfred festival in Sweden. By the end of the year, they had returned twice more, once as main support for the Backyard Babies.
Vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones in 2008

### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
In 2002, they released their first full-length album, _Born a Lion_, produced by Bill Bell, on Bad Taste Records in Europe and on Universal in Canada. The band did several European tours and two Canadian tours to promote the record including a repeat performance at Roskilde and a return to Hultsfred as well as stops to Pukkelpop in Belgium and The Lowlands festival in the Netherlands. They also performed the opening slot with The Rolling Stones on their ["40 Licks" World tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%2240_Licks%22_World_tour "\"40 Licks\" World tour") kick-off show at the Palais Royale in Toronto, Ontario, Canada on August 16, 2002.
In 2003, Danko Jones released their second studio album _We Sweat Blood_, produced by Matt DeMatteo, and saw the group taking a heavier approach to their hard-rock sound.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-9) More touring followed that included Europe and Japan. They were also nominated for two Junos: Best Rock Album (_Born a Lion_) and Best video ("Lovercall"). While success was happening abroad, home relations with Universal Canada had soured and the band was dropped mid-album run. Explanations from the label were vague, but the separation happened after Jones' February 2004 appearance on CBC Sunday where Jones appeared as a pro-downloader opposite then CRIA president, Brian Robertson.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-10) In spite of being dropped from Universal Canada, the group continued to tour heavily for the rest of the year well into 2004 with Turbonegro, Sepultura, and The Bronx. While touring they received another Juno nomination for Best Rock Album (_We Sweat Blood_) and tour Australia as well as more European dates including Rock Am Ring and Rock Im Park in Germany and Download, Leeds and Reading in England.

### 2005–2010: _Sleep Is The Enemy_, _Never Too Loud_ and _Below the Belt_
[edit]
Early 2005 recording sessions for the follow-up to _We Sweat Blood_ were interspersed with a series of tours amidst recording that brought the band to the Netherlands, Germany and South Africa-promoted by their record label and events company ASP Records, who released a collectors double set featuring _Born A Lion_ and _We Sweat Blood_. In April, American label, Razor & Tie released _We Sweat Blood_ and the band set out to America in support as well. Working two releases simultaneously on both sides of the Atlantic proved time-consuming, and the worldwide release of their upcoming studio album, produced by Matt DeMatteo, was pushed back to 2006.
Bassist John Calabrese in 2008
In 2005, Danko Jones signed to Aquarius Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-11) During the summer and fall of 2005, the band toured America heavily with two of _We Sweat Blood_'s singles being played regularly on rock radio in America ("Lovercall" and "Forget My Name"). Stateside tours with Flogging Molly, Our Lady Peace, The Supersuckers, and The (International) Noise Conspiracy followed. Prior to the release of _Sleep Is The Enemy_ drummer Damon Richardson left the band, citing fatigue. He was replaced by Dan Cornelius.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-12)
In January and February 2006, the band set out to do their first Canadian tour in almost four years, opening for Nickelback.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-kilroy-13) On February 17, Danko Jones released _Sleep Is the Enemy_ and went on tour in support of the album, including an American tour and a headlining European club tour with support from Brant Bjork & The Bros.

Formed in 1996, Toronto trio Danko Jones is made up of Danko Jones on guitar/vocals, John “JC” Calabrese on bass and Rich Knox on drums.

# Danko Jones
## Biography
Formed in 1996, Toronto trio Danko Jones is made up of Danko Jones on guitar/vocals, John “JC” Calabrese on bass and Rich Knox on drums.
During the first five years, the band garnered a reputation for their incendiary live shows while releasing singles and eps. They toured with The New Bomb Turks, The Make-Up, The Cold Cold Hearts and Blonde Redhead while playing notable shows with Nashville Pussy, Bratmobile, The Hellacopters, The Dirtbombs and Beck. The band has since toured Europe with The Backyard Babies, Turbonegro, Motorhead and Guns N’ Roses. Touring has taken them to 36 countries on 6 continents. Their 10th studio album “Power Trio” was released in August 2021, including singles such as “I Want Out” which ranked #1 in the German Rock Radio Charts & “Start the Show” with lyrics inspired by the lockdown. The band has also released 3 compilation albums, 2 live albums and made over 30 music videos and guested on Volbeat’s “Black Rose” which hit #1 on billboard Active Rock Radio charts in America.
A quarter of a century without attaching importance to trends and fashions Danko Jones are something of a registered trademark.

**Danko Jones** is a Canadian hard rock band formed in Toronto in 1996, now residing in Stockholm. The band consists of vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones, bassist John "JC" Calabrese and drummer Rich Knox, with Jones and Calabrese remaining the band's only continuous members.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-birch-1) The band's musical style includes elements of hard rock and punk, and they are known for their extensive touring and high-energy live performances, which has earned them acclaim as one of the best live acts in rock music.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-noise-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-3) Danko Jones has released eleven studio albums and been nominated for six Juno Awards.

### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
[edit]
The band was formed in 1996 by Danko Jones (Rishi Ganjoo), Scaltro (John Calabrese) and Gran Sfigato (Michael Caricari), after the former's namesake and initially named Danko Jones And The Impossible Dream.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-:0-5) Danko Jones played consistently for two years after formation in and around the northeastern United States and Canada, opening for The New Bomb Turks, Nashville Pussy, Blonde Redhead, The Make-Up, The Dirtbombs, The Chrome Cranks, and The Demolition Doll Rods. Originally they did not intend to release an album, preferring to have the band's live reputation spread by word of mouth.
Eventually, the trio relented and put out a self-titled six-song EP on Sonic Unyon records in 1998. In 1999, the band performed around Toronto, including at Lee's Palace[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-6) and the Horseshoe Tavern.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-7) That year they released the self-produced _My Love Is Bold_ E.P. and release the single "Bounce". They were nominated for a Juno Award in 2000 for Best Alternative Album.
In early 2000, Danko Jones opened for Beck at Maple Leaf Gardens.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-8) In 2001, Bad Taste Records released a compilation of the band's early recordings, demos, and b-sides entitled, _[I'm Alive and On Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_Alive\_and\_On\_Fire "I'm Alive and On Fire")_. A five-week European tour followed to promote the release including shows at the Roskilde festival in Denmark and Hultsfred festival in Sweden. By the end of the year, they had returned twice more, once as main support for the Backyard Babies.
Vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones in 2008
texts.2:
### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
In 2002, they released their first full-length album, _Born a Lion_, produced by Bill Bell, on Bad Taste Records in Europe and on Universal in Canada. The band did several European tours and two Canadian tours to promote the record including a repeat performance at Roskilde and a return to Hultsfred as well as stops to Pukkelpop in Belgium and The Lowlands festival in the Netherlands. They also performed the opening slot with The Rolling Stones on their ["40 Licks" World tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%2240_Licks%22_World_tour "\"40 Licks\" World tour") kick-off show at the Palais Royale in Toronto, Ontario, Canada on August 16, 2002.
In 2003, Danko Jones released their second studio album _We Sweat Blood_, produced by Matt DeMatteo, and saw the group taking a heavier approach to their hard-rock sound.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-9) More touring followed that included Europe and Japan. They were also nominated for two Junos: Best Rock Album (_Born a Lion_) and Best video ("Lovercall"). While success was happening abroad, home relations with Universal Canada had soured and the band was dropped mid-album run. Explanations from the label were vague, but the separation happened after Jones' February 2004 appearance on CBC Sunday where Jones appeared as a pro-downloader opposite then CRIA president, Brian Robertson.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-10) In spite of being dropped from Universal Canada, the group continued to tour heavily for the rest of the year well into 2004 with Turbonegro, Sepultura, and The Bronx. While touring they received another Juno nomination for Best Rock Album (_We Sweat Blood_) and tour Australia as well as more European dates including Rock Am Ring and Rock Im Park in Germany and Download, Leeds and Reading in England.
texts.3:
### 2005–2010: _Sleep Is The Enemy_, _Never Too Loud_ and _Below the Belt_
[edit]
Early 2005 recording sessions for the follow-up to _We Sweat Blood_ were interspersed with a series of tours amidst recording that brought the band to the Netherlands, Germany and South Africa-promoted by their record label and events company ASP Records, who released a collectors double set featuring _Born A Lion_ and _We Sweat Blood_. In April, American label, Razor & Tie released _We Sweat Blood_ and the band set out to America in support as well. Working two releases simultaneously on both sides of the Atlantic proved time-consuming, and the worldwide release of their upcoming studio album, produced by Matt DeMatteo, was pushed back to 2006.
Bassist John Calabrese in 2008
In 2005, Danko Jones signed to Aquarius Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-11) During the summer and fall of 2005, the band toured America heavily with two of _We Sweat Blood_'s singles being played regularly on rock radio in America ("Lovercall" and "Forget My Name"). Stateside tours with Flogging Molly, Our Lady Peace, The Supersuckers, and The (International) Noise Conspiracy followed. Prior to the release of _Sleep Is The Enemy_ drummer Damon Richardson left the band, citing fatigue. He was replaced by Dan Cornelius.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-12)
In January and February 2006, the band set out to do their first Canadian tour in almost four years, opening for Nickelback.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-kilroy-13) On February 17, Danko Jones released _Sleep Is the Enemy_ and went on tour in support of the album, including an American tour and a headlining European club tour with support from Brant Bjork & The Bros.

## Biography
Formed in 1996, Toronto trio Danko Jones is made up of Danko Jones on guitar/vocals, John “JC” Calabrese on bass and Rich Knox on drums.
During the first five years, the band garnered a reputation for their incendiary live shows while releasing singles and eps. They toured with The New Bomb Turks, The Make-Up, The Cold Cold Hearts and Blonde Redhead while playing notable shows with Nashville Pussy, Bratmobile, The Hellacopters, The Dirtbombs and Beck. The band has since toured Europe with The Backyard Babies, Turbonegro, Motorhead and Guns N’ Roses. Touring has taken them to 36 countries on 6 continents. Their 10th studio album “Power Trio” was released in August 2021, including singles such as “I Want Out” which ranked #1 in the German Rock Radio Charts & “Start the Show” with lyrics inspired by the lockdown. The band has also released 3 compilation albums, 2 live albums and made over 30 music videos and guested on Volbeat’s “Black Rose” which hit #1 on billboard Active Rock Radio charts in America.
A quarter of a century without attaching importance to trends and fashions Danko Jones are something of a registered trademark.

**Danko Jones** is a Canadian hard rock band formed in Toronto in 1996, now residing in Stockholm. The band consists of vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones, bassist John "JC" Calabrese and drummer Rich Knox, with Jones and Calabrese remaining the band's only continuous members.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-birch-1) The band's musical style includes elements of hard rock and punk, and they are known for their extensive touring and high-energy live performances, which has earned them acclaim as one of the best live acts in rock music.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-noise-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-3) Danko Jones has released eleven studio albums and been nominated for six Juno Awards.

### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
[edit]
The band was formed in 1996 by Danko Jones (Rishi Ganjoo), Scaltro (John Calabrese) and Gran Sfigato (Michael Caricari), after the former's namesake and initially named Danko Jones And The Impossible Dream.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-:0-5) Danko Jones played consistently for two years after formation in and around the northeastern United States and Canada, opening for The New Bomb Turks, Nashville Pussy, Blonde Redhead, The Make-Up, The Dirtbombs, The Chrome Cranks, and The Demolition Doll Rods. Originally they did not intend to release an album, preferring to have the band's live reputation spread by word of mouth.
Eventually, the trio relented and put out a self-titled six-song EP on Sonic Unyon records in 1998. In 1999, the band performed around Toronto, including at Lee's Palace[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-6) and the Horseshoe Tavern.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-7) That year they released the self-produced _My Love Is Bold_ E.P. and release the single "Bounce". They were nominated for a Juno Award in 2000 for Best Alternative Album.
In early 2000, Danko Jones opened for Beck at Maple Leaf Gardens.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-8) In 2001, Bad Taste Records released a compilation of the band's early recordings, demos, and b-sides entitled, _[I'm Alive and On Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_Alive\_and\_On\_Fire "I'm Alive and On Fire")_. A five-week European tour followed to promote the release including shows at the Roskilde festival in Denmark and Hultsfred festival in Sweden. By the end of the year, they had returned twice more, once as main support for the Backyard Babies.
Vocalist and guitarist Danko Jones in 2008

### 1996–2004: Formation and early years
In 2002, they released their first full-length album, _Born a Lion_, produced by Bill Bell, on Bad Taste Records in Europe and on Universal in Canada. The band did several European tours and two Canadian tours to promote the record including a repeat performance at Roskilde and a return to Hultsfred as well as stops to Pukkelpop in Belgium and The Lowlands festival in the Netherlands. They also performed the opening slot with The Rolling Stones on their ["40 Licks" World tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%2240_Licks%22_World_tour "\"40 Licks\" World tour") kick-off show at the Palais Royale in Toronto, Ontario, Canada on August 16, 2002.
In 2003, Danko Jones released their second studio album _We Sweat Blood_, produced by Matt DeMatteo, and saw the group taking a heavier approach to their hard-rock sound.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-9) More touring followed that included Europe and Japan. They were also nominated for two Junos: Best Rock Album (_Born a Lion_) and Best video ("Lovercall"). While success was happening abroad, home relations with Universal Canada had soured and the band was dropped mid-album run. Explanations from the label were vague, but the separation happened after Jones' February 2004 appearance on CBC Sunday where Jones appeared as a pro-downloader opposite then CRIA president, Brian Robertson.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-10) In spite of being dropped from Universal Canada, the group continued to tour heavily for the rest of the year well into 2004 with Turbonegro, Sepultura, and The Bronx. While touring they received another Juno nomination for Best Rock Album (_We Sweat Blood_) and tour Australia as well as more European dates including Rock Am Ring and Rock Im Park in Germany and Download, Leeds and Reading in England.

### 2005–2010: _Sleep Is The Enemy_, _Never Too Loud_ and _Below the Belt_
[edit]
Early 2005 recording sessions for the follow-up to _We Sweat Blood_ were interspersed with a series of tours amidst recording that brought the band to the Netherlands, Germany and South Africa-promoted by their record label and events company ASP Records, who released a collectors double set featuring _Born A Lion_ and _We Sweat Blood_. In April, American label, Razor & Tie released _We Sweat Blood_ and the band set out to America in support as well. Working two releases simultaneously on both sides of the Atlantic proved time-consuming, and the worldwide release of their upcoming studio album, produced by Matt DeMatteo, was pushed back to 2006.
Bassist John Calabrese in 2008
In 2005, Danko Jones signed to Aquarius Records.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-11) During the summer and fall of 2005, the band toured America heavily with two of _We Sweat Blood_'s singles being played regularly on rock radio in America ("Lovercall" and "Forget My Name"). Stateside tours with Flogging Molly, Our Lady Peace, The Supersuckers, and The (International) Noise Conspiracy followed. Prior to the release of _Sleep Is The Enemy_ drummer Damon Richardson left the band, citing fatigue. He was replaced by Dan Cornelius.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-12)
In January and February 2006, the band set out to do their first Canadian tour in almost four years, opening for Nickelback.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danko_Jones#cite_note-kilroy-13) On February 17, Danko Jones released _Sleep Is the Enemy_ and went on tour in support of the album, including an American tour and a headlining European club tour with support from Brant Bjork & The Bros.

**Casa Loma** (Spanish for "Hill House") is a Gothic Revivalcastle-style mansion and garden in midtown Toronto, Ontario, Canada, that is now a historic house museum and landmark. It was constructed from 1911 to 1914 as a residence for financier Sir Henry Pellatt. The architect was E.J. Lennox,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-1) who designed several other city landmarks. Casa Loma sits at an elevation of 140 metres (460 ft) above sea level,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-2)66 metres (217 ft) above Lake Ontario.

Due to its unique architectural character in Toronto, Casa Loma has been a popular filming location for movies and television. It is also a popular venue for wedding ceremonies,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-3) and Casa Loma can be rented in the evenings after the museum closes to the public.
Construction of Casa Loma, c. 1912
In 1903, financier Henry Pellatt purchased 25 lots from developers Kertland and Rolf. Pellatt commissioned architect E.J. Lennox to design Casa Loma, with construction beginning in 1911, starting with the massive stables, potting shed and Hunting Lodge (a.k.a. coach-house) a few hundred feet north of the main building. The Hunting Lodge is a two-storey 4,380-square-foot (407 m 2) house with servants' quarters. As soon as the stable complex was completed, Pellatt sold his summer house in Scarborough (burned down in the 1920s[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-4) but the Lennox designed groundskeeper's home at 12 Courcelette Road remains[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-5)) to his son and moved to the Hunting Lodge. The stables were used as a construction site for the mansion (and also served as the quarters for the male servants), with some of the machinery still remaining in the rooms under the stables._[citation needed_]
The house cost about $3.5 million (equivalent to $99.8 million in 2025) and took 299 workers three years to build. Due to the start of World War I, construction was halted. At 98 rooms covering 64,700 square feet, it was the largest private residence in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-6) Notable amenities included an elevator, an oven large enough to cook an ox, two vertical passages for pipe organs, a central vacuum, two secret passages in Pellatt's ground-floor office, a pool, and three bowling lanes in the basement (the last two were never completed).

Most of the third floor was left unfinished, and today serves as the Regimental Museum for [The Queen's Own Rifles of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Queen's_Own_Rifles_of_Canada "The Queen's Own Rifles of Canada"). Pellatt joined the regiment as a rifleman and rose through the ranks to become the commanding officer. He was knighted for his dedication to the regiment. Pellatt later served as the honorary colonel and was promoted to major-general upon retirement.
During the depression that followed the war, the City of Toronto increased Casa Loma's property taxes from $600 per year to $1,000 a month, and Pellatt, already experiencing financial difficulties, auctioned off $1.5 million in art and $250,000 in furnishings. Pellatt was able to enjoy life in the mansion for less than ten years, leaving in 1923.
In late 1920s, investors operated Casa Loma for a short time as a luxury hotel. During Prohibition, it became a popular nightspot for wealthy Americans. The Orange Blossoms, later known as Glen Gray and the Casa Loma Orchestra, played there for eight months in 1927–1928. Shortly thereafter, they went on a tour of North America and became a major swing era dance band.
Lieutenant-Governor Herbert Bruce opens Casa Loma to the public, 1937.

The city seized Casa Loma in 1924 for unpaid taxes, and for years, the building was left vacant.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-Globe-7) In the 1930s, CFRB broadcaster Claire Wallace spent a night at Casa Loma to gather material for a story about ghosts and supernatural phenomena, and she later broadcast an appeal to save the building from demolition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-:0-8) Her broadcast was heard by the vice-president of a local Kiwanis Club,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-:0-8) and subsequently Casa Loma was leased in 1937 by the Kiwanis Club of West Toronto, later the Kiwanis Club of Casa Loma (KCCL), which began operating the mansion under a sole-source contract as a tourist destination.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-Globe-7)
Tour guide stands in front of Casa Loma in the mid twentieth century
During World War II, the stables were used to conceal research and production of sonar, and for construction of sonar devices (known as ASDIC) for U-boat detection, according to a book about the "castle". The area was closed, behind an "Under Repairs" sign. The suggestion that the stables were under renovation allowed workers of the secret facility to come and go without suspicion.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-9) Casa Loma is often claimed to be the location of Station M that manufactured covert devices for agents, claiming that the book _Inside Camp X_ provides this information.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-10) In 2015, however, author Lynn Philip Hodgson rejected this in an interview with the _Toronto Star_. "Nobody knows where Station M was. You won't read where it was in any book."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-11)

### Vintage car exhibition
It also appeared in the television adaptation of R. L. Stine's _Goosebumps_ series' _A Night In Terror Tower_. Casa Loma also features prominently in the biography-documentary of Sir Henry Pellatt, _The Pellatt Newsreel: the Man who Built Casa Loma_, which was nominated for a 2009 Gemini for Best Biography Documentary.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-24) TV show _Hemlock Grove_ was also filmed there as well as _The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones_ and related _Shadowhunters._
Exterior shots of the building were used in the Gothic TV show _Strange Paradise_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-25)
It is also the filming location of the 2016 TV film _[The Rocky Horror Picture Show: Let's Do the Time Warp Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rocky\_Horror\_Picture\_Show:\_Let's\_Do\_the\_Time\_Warp\_Again "The Rocky Horror Picture Show: Let's Do the Time Warp Again")_, where scenes at Dr. Frank N. Furter's castle and the movie theatre where the audience participated were filmed. Ivy Levan's performance of the song "Science Fiction Double Feature" was filmed at Casa Loma (a movie theatre marquee was placed at the front entrance of the castle for filming).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-26)
In 2018, Casa Loma served as a filming location for the 2019 American black comedythriller_Ready or Not_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-27)
In 2022, Casa Loma was the filming location of the music video for _Wait for U_ by Future and Drake.
In 2025, _Top Chef: Destination Canada_ filmed the Episode 4 Elimination challenge at Casa Loma.
In 2026, Casa Loma was one of the filming locations for the Team Challenge of the eleventh episode of _MasterChef: Global Gauntlet_.

**Casa Loma** (Spanish for "Hill House") is a Gothic Revivalcastle-style mansion and garden in midtown Toronto, Ontario, Canada, that is now a historic house museum and landmark. It was constructed from 1911 to 1914 as a residence for financier Sir Henry Pellatt. The architect was E.J. Casa Loma sits at an elevation of 140 metres (460 ft) above sea level,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-2)66 metres (217 ft) above Lake Ontario.

Due to its unique architectural character in Toronto, Casa Loma has been a popular filming location for movies and television. It is also a popular venue for wedding ceremonies,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-3) and Casa Loma can be rented in the evenings after the museum closes to the public.

In 1903, financier Henry Pellatt purchased 25 lots from developers Kertland and Rolf. Pellatt commissioned architect E.J. Lennox to design Casa Loma, with construction beginning in 1911, starting with the massive stables, potting shed and Hunting Lodge (a.k.a. coach-house) a few hundred feet north of the main building. The Hunting Lodge is a two-storey 4,380-square-foot (407 m 2) house with servants' quarters. As soon as the stable complex was completed, Pellatt sold his summer house in Scarborough (burned down in the 1920s[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-4) but the Lennox designed groundskeeper's home at 12 Courcelette Road remains[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-5)) to his son and moved to the Hunting Lodge. The stables were used as a construction site for the mansion (and also served as the quarters for the male servants), with some of the machinery still remaining in the rooms under the stables._[citation needed_]
The house cost about $3.5 million (equivalent to $99.8 million in 2025) and took 299 workers three years to build. Due to the start of World War I, construction was halted. At 98 rooms covering 64,700 square feet, it was the largest private residence in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Loma#cite_note-6) Notable amenities included an elevator, an oven large enough to cook an ox, two vertical passages for pipe organs, a central vacuum, two secret passages in Pellatt's ground-floor office, a pool, and three bowling lanes in the basement (the last two were never completed).

Pellatt joined the regiment as a rifleman and rose through the ranks to become the commanding officer. He was knighted for his dedication to the regiment. Pellatt later served as the honorary colonel and was promoted to major-general upon retirement.
